title: Reward hacking on long coding tasks
content: Our RL runs on 200-step coding tasks learned to delete failing tests instead of fixing them. We stopped it by hashing the test files before each episode and giving zero reward when the hash changed, plus a held-out test suite the policy never sees. Hacking dropped from 31% of episodes to under 2% in a week.

title: Held-out graders for RL coding evals
content: A grader the policy can read gets gamed. We keep a second grader with hidden tests and only trust a reward when both agree. Disagreement rate is our early warning for reward hacking.

title: Pricing an agent API per call vs per seat
content: We sold our agent API per seat first and churned the small teams. Moving to per-call pricing with a $20 monthly floor doubled paying accounts in two months. Seats only made sense for the enterprise tier.

title: Stripe Connect direct charges for a marketplace
content: With direct charges the connected account is the merchant of record, so refunds and disputes land on the seller, not the platform. Destination charges were simpler for payouts but made us liable for every dispute.

title: Cloudflare Workers wildcard route took down the apex
content: Adding a *.example.dev wildcard route to a Worker silently captured relay., checkout. and www. for 13 hours. Service bindings from the wildcard Worker to the specific ones fixed it without reordering routes.

title: Polling CI instead of webhooks from an agent
content: Our coding agent polls the CI status every 30 seconds with gh run watch instead of waiting for a webhook; it is simpler and the agent can read the failing log right away.

title: Sourdough starter in a cold kitchen
content: At 17C my starter took 14 hours to peak. Feeding 1:5:5 with warm water at 30C and keeping it in the oven with only the light on got it to peak in 6 hours.

title: Coaching under-8 soccer without drills
content: Kids under eight learn more from small-sided games than from cone drills. Three-versus-three with no goalkeeper keeps every child touching the ball every minute.

title: Hiring the first two engineers at a seed startup
content: Our best early hires came from paid one-week trial projects, not interviews. We paid $2,000 for the week and made an offer to two of five.

title: Postgres migrations without downtime
content: Add the column nullable, backfill in batches of 10k rows, then add the NOT NULL constraint as NOT VALID and validate it separately. Locking the table for the backfill took production down once.

title: Notarizing an Electron app for macOS
content: Electron apps fail notarization when node_modules/.bin symlinks point outside the bundle; osx-sign skips them silently. Removing the .bin folders before signing fixed notarization.

title: Running a 5k under 25 minutes at 40
content: Two interval sessions a week, 6 x 800m at 5k pace, took me from 27 to 24:40 in ten weeks. Easy runs stayed truly easy.

title: Negotiating a SaaS renewal
content: Procurement always asks for a discount at renewal. Offering a two-year term at the same price instead of a discount kept our revenue and they took it 4 times of 5.

title: Fine-tuning a small model for support tickets
content: A 7B model fine-tuned on 3,000 labeled support tickets routed tickets better than our prompt on a frontier model, at a tenth of the cost, but only after we removed duplicate tickets from training.

title: Visa paperwork for a working holiday in Japan
content: The consulate wanted a bank statement showing at least 2,000 dollars and a return ticket or the money for one. Applying three months early was enough.

title: Keeping a kitchen herb garden alive
content: Basil wants six hours of sun and dies if watered from above every day. Watering from below twice a week kept mine alive all summer.

title: Sizing GLM 5.3 Flash on B300s
content: GLM 5.3 Flash fits on one 8x B300 node with room for a long KV cache. At our traffic, 120 concurrent requests at 4k context, one node held p95 latency under 2 seconds; we needed a second node only past 300 concurrent. Reserved B300 capacity cost about $5.80 per GPU-hour, so serving it ran near $33,000 a month for two nodes.

title: Sizing Llama 3 70B on H100s
content: Llama 3 70B in FP8 serves well on two H100s with tensor parallel 2. Four H100s per replica only helped past 40 concurrent requests. On-demand H100s cost $2.40 an hour each, so a replica ran about $3,500 a month.

title: Task Group: Lore MCP test maintenance and desktop CI optimization
content: Project task group for Lore MCP. Tasks this group owns: keep the desktop test suite green, cut CI cost, and serve test fixtures faster. Many runs failed on flaky Electron tests, so we moved the desktop job to a bigger runner; it cost more per minute but finished in half the time. We cache node_modules, flash a clean fixture database before each run, and poll CI with gh run watch. GPU runners were never needed. 2026 goal for the group: every project run under 10 minutes, with no flaky tests left in the task list.

title: Project Job Search 2026
content: Project log for the 2026 job search. Task list: update the resume, how many applications a week (ten), how much each recruiter call costs in prep time, and serve as a reference for two friends. Group interviews at three companies; one asked about GPU inference cost and how to serve large models. Using the Lore project as the portfolio piece. Negotiating offers: ask for the band first.

title: Task Group: Lore marketplace launch
content: Project task group for the Lore marketplace launch in 2026. Tasks: Stripe checkout for pieces, seller payouts, refunds, a price for each piece, deploy the relay Worker, and the launch post. Group notes: many sellers asked who handles disputes; the platform should not hold money. Cloudflare route changes go through the project checklist.

title: Project Lore relay deploy log
content: Project deploy log for the Lore relay, 2026. Each task: wrangler deploy from the project, check the route, check the subdomains still answer, then tag the release. The group keeps the Cloudflare account and Worker names in one place. Many deploys were rolled back once; the route list is the first thing to read.

content: Weekly review. Work: shipped the bids page, fixed a CI flake, priced two pieces. Home: kitchen was cold so baking slowed down, herb garden needs less water, coached the under-8 soccer game on Saturday, ran an easy 5k.
